column1: # Shell commands the read-only agents may and may not run, checked by run.py
#             qa-tester, "reviewers" for the three git-only agents, or "all"
#   hook      A (allowed) or D (denied) by the hook in that agent's mode
#   opencode  A or D under that agent's OpenCode rules, or - to skip: run.py
#             matches the whole command string, while OpenCode checks each
#             subcommand of a compound command separately (and refuses
#             commands its scanner can't analyze), so some cases only hold there
#   command   the rest of the line, as is (a literal tab stays a tab); <NL>,
# Add a case for every bypass found, so it can't come back. Not needed: git
# ^ is only risky with zsh's extended_glob (off): the hook refuses it anyway.
# "git diff*" in OpenCode let this through: difftool runs rm on the work tree.
# The scanners are the auditor's only.
# Subprojects: --cwd / --prefix / -C in the hook, the working directory in OpenCode.
# Rewriting sources, writing files anywhere, running other programs.
# make: one target, nothing else (in OpenCode not even -k / -jN).
# Same expansion and chaining rules as the other agents.
